answers.solution:
SYMPTOM: `gitreins guard` passes in your shell, but `git commit` is REFUSED by the gitreins pre-commit hook re-running the guard - the hook's guard fails on an environmental precondition (e.g. 'ERROR: DuckBrain URL missing - set DUCKBRAIN_URL before running the live gate'), exit_code=2, first_failing_test: none detected.

WHY: the pre-commit hook process does not reliably inherit variables you `export`ed in an earlier shell call/turn (each tool call may be a fresh shell); it runs the guard with a clean environment, so any guard precondition that depends on an env var (live-gate URLs, API keys) fails at commit time even though the manual run was green.

FIX (verified in repo auger, tick 2026-11-21): prefix the assignment to the git invocation itself so the hook inherits it:
    DUCKBRAIN_URL=http://<ip-address>:3000 git commit -F <msgfile>
Environment assignments on the same command line are inherited by the git process and by its child hook.

DIAGNOSIS: compare the newest .gitreins/logs/guard-*.log written by the COMMIT attempt against the green manual one - if the only difference is the env-precondition ERROR inside the tests step (fast exit, no test dots), it is the env var, not the code. The commit attempt writes its own guard log timestamped seconds after your green run.

VERIFY: the commit proceeds; the hook guard reaches real test execution (progress dots in the guard log) instead of exiting at the precondition.
